title: Why This Tiny Jellyfish Is Much Worse Than You Think
format: Vertical 9:16 TikTok cross-post (native 270x480 at <=480p, 30 fps). Green-screen talking head (creator cut out, holding a lav mic like a reporter) composited over still stock photos, with every spoken sentence burned in as a centred white caption card. Very early 'Casual Geographic' / Mndiaye_97 style: deadpan, slightly comedic tone delivering horrifying animal facts.
transcript_source: No YouTube auto-subs; faster-whisper small on Spark CPU (word timestamps), cross-checked against burned-in captions. Full text: research/library/transcripts/jw6bS-WL4F4.txt

title_pattern.template: Why This [Tiny/Cute/Harmless-looking X] Is Much Worse Than You Think
devices: 'This' demonstrative: implies the viewer is looking at it right now (works with the frame/thumbnail)
'Than You Think' challenges the viewer's existing belief, a mild myth-bust curiosity gap
subject not named (Irukandji is unsearchable/unknown), so the title sells the contrast instead of the noun
title_pattern.notes: The YouTube title differs from the on-video hook ('The Most Dangerous Animal in Australia can make you Su1c!dal'). Title is the soft, search/browse-friendly framing; the video hook is the harder, shock framing. On-screen text uses leetspeak censorship (Su1c!dal, hom1c1dal) to dodge TikTok moderation, which also reads as edgy.

thumbnail.composition: Not a designed thumbnail: YouTube auto-frame from ~34 s, a vertical frame pillarboxed in a 16:9 canvas with blurred brownish side bars. In the vertical frame: a glowing cyan box jellyfish top-centre-right over dark green particle-filled water, tentacles hanging down; the creator cut-out bottom-left (cap backwards, mic in hand) at about 40% of frame height; white caption block centre-right.
thumbnail.text: Burned caption: 'Because one of the symptoms of being stung by this tiny jellyfish is an impending feeling of doom' (white sans, thin dark shadow, 5 centred lines).
thumbnail.colours: Dark bottle-green underwater background with bokeh specks; luminous pale cyan jellyfish bell is the brightest object; warm skin tones and a red cap band on the presenter; white text.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: The jellyfish is shown about the size of the presenter's head, i.e. enlarged; the 'tiny' claim is carried by the text, not the image.
thumbnail.why_it_works: On Shorts the thumbnail matters little (feed autoplay). The frame that was picked happens to contain the single most unusual fact (a sting that causes a 'feeling of doom'), a glowing creature on dark, and a human face, so even as a static it reads as 'creepy fact + person reacting'.

hook.verbatim_first_5s: (0.0 s, no intro, speech starts on frame 1) 'Most dangerous animal in Australia can make you suicidal.' (2.9 s) 'Australia is a country with venomous snakes, rabbits that went to prison, an actual devil...'
hook.on_screen_text_0_3s: 'The Most Dangerous Animal in Australia can make you Su1c!dal' in TikTok-native white rounded caption boxes with black text, top third, over a plain selfie shot in a bedroom.
hook.device: Superlative + shocking consequence in one sentence ('most dangerous' + 'make you suicidal'): the consequence is psychological, not physical, which is unexpected and creates an open loop that is only paid off at 31-40 s. Then an immediate comic list of Australia's threats (snakes, imprisoned rabbits, devils, cassowary-as-dinosaur) that lowers the guard and builds a 'which one is it?' tease, before the twist 'But the deadliest of them all is in the ocean'.

beats.summary: Most dangerous animal in Australia can make you suicidal. Selfie shot, TikTok text boxes; the only shot without a composite background.
Australia's threats as a joke list: venomous snakes, rabbits 'that went to prison', a real devil, and a 'dinosaur' (cassowary). Four-photo collage behind the presenter.
'But the deadliest of them all is in the ocean.' Same collage; caption switches. Pivot from land list to the real subject.
Names the Irukandji: most venomous thing on the planet yet small enough to never see coming. Photo of the jellyfish next to an Australian $2 coin for scale.
Venom 100x worse than a cobra's and 1000x more potent than a tarantula's; thousands of cells inject you. Same coin photo, presenter jumps to the other side.
Muscle cramps, burning face, vomiting, nausea, headaches. Big macro jellyfish photo.
Victims say it feels like being branded with a hot iron, 'and that's exactly what the scars look like' -> photo of welted, branded-looking legs.
'But that's not the worst part': the sting causes an impending feeling of doom so strong patients beg doctors to end their life. Pays off the 'suicidal' hook at 54-70% of runtime.
All of this in as little as five minutes; if you're swimming you lose control of your body and sink to your death.
Can cause brain haemorrhage, 'meaning you bleed from your brain' (plain-English restatement of jargon).
If treated quickly you'll survive, but you'll be traumatized for life. Specimen-in-vial photo.

In a place where everything evolved to kill you, 'this homicidal sperm cell is the biggest op of all'. Callback to the Australia framing plus a memorable insult-metaphor for the shape; video ends on the line, no CTA, which loops cleanly.

pacing.words_per_minute_note: Very fast, near-continuous delivery; longest pause between sentences ~0.7 s. Typical of 2021 TikTok fact videos.
pacing.avg_shot_length_note: Backgrounds (stills) hold ~6.4 s on average, but something visibly changes every ~3.4 s: 17 caption cards plus 2 presenter jump-repositions. Caption card = one spoken sentence.

techniques_worth_copying: Hook names a superlative AND an unexpected consequence category ('most dangerous' + 'makes you suicidal'): the oddness of the consequence, not the danger, is the curiosity gap. Hold the payoff until ~55% of runtime behind a 'But that's not the worst part' re-hook.

Misdirection list before the real subject: list 3-4 famous/funny candidates in a land-based category, then pivot ('But the deadliest of them all is in the ocean'). Comic specifics (rabbits that went to prison, cassowary = dinosaur) buy goodwill before the horror.
Scale proof with a familiar object (coin next to the creature) the moment the 'tiny' claim is made.
Comparative stat stack with known villains ('100x worse than a cobra, 1000x more potent than a tarantula').

Escalation ladder of symptoms, each step worse: pain list -> branding scars (visual proof) -> psychological doom -> death by drowning -> brain bleeding. Each beat starts with an escalator word ('Next', 'But that's not the worst part', 'And', 'The sting is so severe').
Restate jargon in blunt plain English immediately ('brain hemorrhaging, meaning you bleed from your brain').

Relief beat then a comic insult-metaphor button that calls back to the opening frame ('In a place where everything evolved to kill you, this homicidal sperm cell is the biggest op of all'). No CTA, so it loops.
Every sentence becomes its own centred caption card; background only changes when the subject changes, so the caption swap carries the visual rhythm cheaply.
Presenter position jump (left -> right) used as a 'cut' when the background image needs to stay.

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: High for structure and layout; the look is mostly 'caption card + layered stills', which is trivially reproducible in Remotion. The human green-screen presenter is the one element that cannot be copied (no AI video, no real footage); replace with an illustrated mascot/character or drop the presenter and let the creature illustration take the frame.
needs: Vertical 1080x1920 composition: top/centre caption zone + illustrated background layer + optional character layer bottom-left/right that can jump sides on beat changes.

Sentence-level caption cards: white sans (e.g. Inter/Proxima-style semibold), thin dark shadow, centred, auto-shrink for long lines, swapped exactly on TTS sentence boundaries; plus a TikTok-style rounded white box variant for the hook card.

SVG creature illustrations: translucent box jellyfish (bell with gradient, inner glow, beaded tentacles with gentle sine sway), a 'tiny' version beside a coin for scale, macro bell close-up, specimen in a vial/jar.
SVG 2x2 'threat collage' panel for the misdirection list (snake, rabbit in prison stripes, devil, cassowary-as-dinosaur silhouette) to keep the comic beat.
Underwater backgrounds: dark green/black gradient with drifting bokeh particles (Canvas or SVG circles with blur), slight Ken Burns zoom on each still to add motion the original lacks.
Stat callouts for '100x cobra' / '1000x tarantula' as animated counters or side-by-side icons.
Symptom escalation visual: body silhouette with lighting-up regions (face burn, muscles, head) and a stylised welt pattern instead of the real scar photo.
Fast TTS (Kokoro) at ~250-270 wpm with minimal pauses, ~0.5 s caption-less breath before major image changes.
Censor-style text option (leetspeak for words like suicidal/homicidal) as a caption filter only if targeting TikTok.
